title: Tensor networks meet machine learning
description: A companion to our short video: why the low-rank structure behind quantum many-body physics also appears in data, and what tensor-network models can and cannot yet do.

video.caption: A narrated tour from the area law and tensor trains, through network compression, MPS classifiers and Born machines, to quantum circuits and open questions.

sections.heading: Two fields, one representation problem
paragraphs: A wave function of N spins has 2^N amplitudes. A binary image with 784 pixels lives in a space of 2^784 configurations. Quantum many-body physics and machine learning both need to describe functions on spaces this large using a manageable number of parameters.

A tensor network writes one huge tensor as a contraction of many small ones. Each small tensor carries a few physical indices and a few bond indices shared with its neighbours; summing over the bonds rebuilds the whole. The bond dimension D controls how much correlation the network can carry, and so how many parameters it needs.

The same object has appeared under different names. Numerical analysts call the one-dimensional chain a tensor train; physicists call it a matrix product state, or MPS. The DMRG algorithm, which optimizes an MPS by sweeping back and forth and updating a few tensors at a time, has close relatives among alternating optimization methods for tensor trains.

sections.heading: Why low rank can work
paragraphs: Most states in Hilbert space are highly entangled, yet ground states of gapped local Hamiltonians are not. Their entanglement across a cut grows with the size of the boundary rather than the volume: an area law. In one dimension this has been proven, and it is why an MPS with modest bond dimension describes such states accurately. Critical systems and higher dimensions need more care.

Natural images are also special. Meaningful pictures occupy a tiny corner of configuration space, far from uniform noise. One way to quantify this is the mutual information between two parts of an image. For a Born machine built from an MPS, the mutual information across a cut is at most log₂ D bits, so a data set with little mutual information across every cut can, in principle, be captured with small bonds.

The estimates shown in the video for binarized MNIST come out at only a few bits, far below the hundreds allowed in principle. That is encouraging, but it is not the whole story. An MPS orders pixels along a line, so neighbouring pixels in two dimensions can end up far apart in the chain. This is one motivation for tree and two-dimensional networks.

sections.heading: Compressing and relating neural networks
paragraphs: Tensor networks first entered deep learning as a compression tool. A dense weight matrix can be reshaped into a high-order tensor and written as a matrix product operator. Novikov and coauthors showed that fully connected layers of large image classifiers can be compressed by several orders of magnitude with only a small change in accuracy. In our work on MPO-Net, we applied the same decomposition to both fully connected and convolutional layers.

The connection also runs the other way. Restricted Boltzmann machines can be rewritten exactly as tensor network states, with a bond dimension set by their connectivity, while not every tensor network state has an efficient Boltzmann-machine form. Related results link convolutional and recurrent architectures to hierarchical Tucker and tensor-train formats. These correspondences let ideas about expressive power move between the two fields.

sections.heading: Tensor networks as learning models
paragraphs: Tensor networks can also be the model itself. Stoudenmire and Schwab mapped each pixel to a two-component feature vector, so that an image becomes a product state, and represented the classifier as an MPS acting on it. Trained with DMRG-style sweeps, it reached a test error below one percent on MNIST. Later tree, PEPS, string-bond and residual architectures reported results comparable to classic convolutional baselines on Fashion-MNIST.

For generative modelling, the Born rule gives a natural recipe: the probability of a configuration is its squared amplitude divided by a normalization constant. For an MPS or a tree tensor network, that constant is an exact contraction, and samples can be drawn directly pixel by pixel from conditional probabilities without a Markov chain. For PEPS, contraction is generally approximate.

Han and coauthors trained an MPS Born machine on binarized MNIST and reported a test negative log-likelihood of about 101.5. Our tree tensor network model captured more two-dimensional correlation and lowered this value; later PEPS and autoregressive MPS models went further, approaching strong deep generative models such as PixelCNN, though not yet surpassing the best of them.

sections.heading: Towards quantum circuits, and what remains open
paragraphs: If each tensor is made unitary, a tensor network becomes a quantum circuit. Huggins and coauthors proposed discriminative and generative tensor-network circuits that could run on small quantum processors, trained with hybrid quantum-classical optimization. This makes tensor-network models a natural bridge between machine learning and quantum computing.

Several questions remain open. We still lack good ways to measure which structure in a data set suits which network geometry. The expressive power and learnability of different architectures are only partly understood, and the optimizers used in practice leave room for improvement. Tensor network models are also costly: contraction cost grows as a power of the bond dimension.

In return, they are unusually interpretable. Canonical forms, entanglement spectra and exact normalization give handles that most neural networks lack. Much of the bridge between the two fields is still waiting to be built.

zh.title: 当张量网络遇见机器学习
zh.description: 配合我们短片的一篇文章：量子多体物理背后的低秩结构为何也出现在数据中，以及张量网络模型目前能做什么、还做不到什么。
zh.videoCaption: 从面积律与张量链出发，经由网络压缩、MPS 分类器与玻恩机，一路讲到量子线路与尚待解决的问题。

sections.heading: 两个领域，同一个表示问题
paragraphs: N 个自旋的波函数有 2^N 个振幅；一张 784 像素的二值图像，则处在 2^784 种组态构成的空间中。量子多体物理和机器学习都需要用数量可控的参数，去描述定义在如此巨大空间上的函数。
张量网络把一个巨大的张量写成许多小张量的缩并。每个小张量带有少量物理指标，以及少量与近邻共享的键指标；对所有键求和，就重建出整体。键维数 D 决定网络能够承载多少关联，也因此决定需要多少参数。
同一个对象曾以不同的名字出现。数值分析学者把一维链称为张量链（tensor train），物理学家称之为矩阵乘积态（MPS）。DMRG 算法通过来回扫描、每次更新少数几个张量来优化 MPS，它与张量链的交替优化方法有着密切的亲缘关系。

sections.heading: 低秩为什么可行
paragraphs: 希尔伯特空间中的绝大多数态都高度纠缠，但有能隙的局域哈密顿量的基态并非如此。它们跨过一个切面的纠缠随边界大小而不是体积增长，这就是面积律。一维情形下这一点已被严格证明，这也是键维数适中的 MPS 能够精确描述这类态的原因。临界系统和更高维度则需要更加小心。
自然图像同样特殊。有意义的图片只占组态空间中极小的一角，远离均匀噪声。衡量这一点的一种方式，是图像两部分之间的互信息。对于由 MPS 构成的玻恩机，跨过一个切面的互信息至多为 log₂ D 比特；因此，如果一个数据集在每个切面上的互信息都很小，原则上就可以用小的键维数来刻画。
短片中给出的二值化 MNIST 估计值只有几个比特，远低于原则上允许的数百比特。这令人鼓舞，但并非全部。MPS 把像素排成一条线，二维中相邻的像素在链上可能相距很远。这正是发展树状网络和二维网络的动机之一。

sections.heading: 压缩神经网络，关联神经网络
paragraphs: 张量网络最初作为一种压缩工具进入深度学习。一个稠密权重矩阵可以重塑成高阶张量，再写成矩阵乘积算符。Novikov 等人表明，大型图像分类网络的全连接层可以被压缩几个数量级，而准确率只发生很小的变化。在 MPO-Net 的工作中，我们把同样的分解用于全连接层和卷积层。
这种联系也可以反过来看。受限玻尔兹曼机可以精确改写为张量网络态，其键维数由连接方式决定；而并非每个张量网络态都有高效的玻尔兹曼机形式。相关结果还把卷积网络和循环网络分别与层级 Tucker 格式和张量链格式联系起来。这些对应关系，让关于表达能力的想法得以在两个领域之间流动。

sections.heading: 张量网络作为学习模型
paragraphs: 张量网络也可以就是模型本身。Stoudenmire 与 Schwab 把每个像素映射为一个二分量特征向量，于是一张图像变成一个直积态，再用作用在它上面的 MPS 表示分类器。用类似 DMRG 的扫描训练后，它在 MNIST 上的测试错误率低于百分之一。此后的树状、PEPS、弦键态和残差结构，在 Fashion-MNIST 上报告了与经典卷积基准相当的结果。
对于生成建模，玻恩规则给出了一种自然的方案：一个组态的概率等于其振幅的平方除以归一化常数。对于 MPS 或树张量网络，这个常数是一次精确缩并，而且可以根据条件概率逐个像素直接采样，不需要马尔可夫链。对于 PEPS，缩并一般只能近似进行。
Han 等人在二值化 MNIST 上训练了 MPS 玻恩机，报告的测试负对数似然约为 101.5。我们的树张量网络模型刻画了更多二维关联，降低了这一数值；之后的 PEPS 和自回归 MPS 模型更进一步，接近 PixelCNN 等强大的深度生成模型，但尚未超越其中最好的模型。

sections.heading: 走向量子线路，以及尚待解决的问题
paragraphs: 如果让每个张量都是幺正的，张量网络就变成一个量子线路。Huggins 等人提出了可以在小型量子处理器上运行的判别式与生成式张量网络线路，用量子—经典混合优化来训练。这使张量网络模型成为连接机器学习与量子计算的一座天然桥梁。
仍有几个问题有待解决。我们还缺乏好的方法来衡量数据集中的哪种结构适合哪种网络几何。不同结构的表达能力和可学习性只得到了部分理解，实践中所用的优化器也还有改进空间。张量网络模型的代价也不低：缩并开销随键维数的幂次增长。
作为回报，它们具有少见的可解释性。正则形式、纠缠谱和精确归一化，提供了大多数神经网络所没有的抓手。两个领域之间的这座桥，还有很大一部分等待建造。
